reasoning: Both are solid and handle every input. A meets the rubric more closely: fixed per-role text sizes with no TextScaled, a drawn padlock with an 'Lv' badge, a pressed state on tiles, focus restored on close, and an open button clear of the top bar and the thumbstick and jump corners. B uses TextScaled for the info bar, opts the tappable backdrop out of the safe area, and has no pressed state on tiles. A's truncated diff adds some uncertainty, but its visible code is stronger.

criteria.criterion: Every action works with every input
criteria.note: Tiles, the close button and BlocksButton all fire on Activated; the doc's table gives touch, mouse/keyboard and controller paths, and the B/Y CAS actions are named in InventoryUI (their bodies are cut off in the diff).

An effect defers selectDefaultTile to set GuiService.SelectedObject on the picked tile; the panel has SelectionGroup and Stop behaviors; CLOSE_ACTION exists for B, and close restores the earlier selection.

The HUD button is 88x92 at top right, offset 16 px below the top bar; tiles are 98x86 or 120x140; close is 44 or 56; the panel is sized to Screen.usableSize, and no IgnoreGuiInset appears in the visible code.
Locked tiles show a drawn padlock plus a 'Lv N' badge, 'x0' shows in gray, and pressing a locked tile shakes it and sets the detail strip to 'Unlocks at level N.'
Name, count and lock show on every tile; hover only previews the detail strip, which a tap or selection also fills; there is a pressed sink and a 'Picked' outline and tag.
Fixed TextSize per role comes from Metrics (body 18–24, no TextScaled), on dark panels; badge text at 14–16 is a little small.
InventoryState sources update from Changed and BlockTypeChanged, and all text is bound; the connections are module-level rather than scope-cleaned, which is acceptable for a long-lived module.

A small BlockPlacer change makes number keys refuse locked blocks; the luau-lsp failure is a path-resolution problem; part of the diff (InventoryUI, Theme, Screen) is truncated, so the end-to-end wiring isn't fully visible.

criteria.criterion: Every action works with every input
criteria.note: Tiles, the open button and the close button use Activated; CAS binds B and ButtonY to toggle and ButtonB to close; the doc table covers every input.

selectTileForGamepad sets SelectedObject after a deferred frame; the panel has SelectionGroup and Stop behaviors; B is bound at High priority; the close button is not selectable, and an auto-close when SelectedObject is cleared is a bit hacky.
The open button is 64 px tall at bottom center inside DeviceSafeInsets, and close is 48; but the backdrop ScreenGui, which closes the screen when tapped, uses ScreenInsets.None.
The lock cover shows a 🔒 emoji, 'Level N' and the name, and a count of 0 shows as '0'; pressing a locked tile shakes it and the info bar names the unlock level.

Name, count and lock show on each tile, plus an equipped tick and outline; focus is tied to hover only on keyboard and mouse; there is a press scale only on the open button, and tiles show no pressed state.
Fixed sizes on most labels, but the Info label uses TextScaled with MinTextSize 12, and the lock-cover name is 14 px.
A revision source ticks on Changed, and selectedName follows BlockTypeChanged; everything is bound through derive; the connections are module-level.
Works as described, and BlockPlacer is untouched apart from setEnabled calls; the luau-lsp failure is a path-resolution problem.

strengths: Thorough design: a detail strip, reduced-motion support and the player's transparency setting are respected
Locked tiles have strong non-color cues and give feedback when pressed
Gamepad focus is managed, stays in the panel and is restored on close
Fixed per-role text sizes with compact and regular layouts
weaknesses: Diff truncated, so the key bindings and the mount code couldn't be checked

strengths: Picking a block closes the screen, which suits kids switching blocks
Two ScreenGuis keep the panel in the safe area while the backdrop dims the whole screen
The input mode is tracked live, and hints and selection follow it
weaknesses: Tiles have no pressed state; the auto-close when selection is cleared is fragile
Relies on an emoji for the lock
